title: Mark Our Place Act
official_summary:
Mark Our Place Act

This act authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs to furnish a headstone, marker, or medallion signifying the status of a deceased member of the Armed Forces as a Medal of Honor recipient regardless of when the member served. Under current law, only Medal of Honor recipients who served after 1917 are eligible for such markers.

summary.headline: New law lets the VA provide Medal of Honor headstones, markers, or medallions for recipients from any era, not just those who served after 1917.
summary.what_it_does: The law allows the Department of Veterans Affairs to provide a headstone, marker, or medallion showing that a deceased service member received the Medal of Honor, no matter when they served. Before this law, only Medal of Honor recipients who served after 1917 could get these special markers.

who_it_affects.group: Families of Medal of Honor recipients who served before 1917
who_it_affects.how: They can now get a VA headstone, marker, or medallion that shows their relative's Medal of Honor status.
The VA gains authority to furnish Medal of Honor markers for recipients from earlier eras, such as the Civil War.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 25, 2024; the summary does not list a separate start date.
